name: Botswana
summary: A light blue field with a black horizontal band edged in white. Adopted at independence in 1966, it is one of few African flags that do not use the Pan-African colours or the colours of a political party.
origin: Bechuanaland became independent as Botswana on 30 September 1966. The new flag deliberately avoided the colours of the ruling Botswana Democratic Party and of the opposition, to emphasise national unity.

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: Water and rain; reflects the national motto 'Pula', meaning 'rain'.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The Black majority, in racial harmony with the white minority.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The white minority; together with black, racial harmony. Also the zebra, the national animal.

facts: Botswana's currency is called the pula, the same word as the national motto.
The black and white stripes are often linked to the zebra on the coat of arms.
Estonia's flag also has light blue, black and white.
clues: Light blue with a black band edged in white.
Its blue reflects a motto meaning 'rain'.
Its black and white bands are linked to a striped national animal.
